blocks.title: fiercely independent
blocks.html:
adverb + adjective

  • My mother is 84 and still fiercely independent — she refuses to let anyone help.
  • The newspaper has stayed fiercely independent through three changes of owner.
  • Adolescents are fiercely independent in theory and deeply conformist in practice.

CA: ferotgement independent

ES: ferozmente independiente

'Fiercely' intensifies effortful qualities: loyal, protective, competitive, proud. Not *fiercely tired.

blocks.title: come across as
blocks.html:
phrasal verb + complement

  • He comes across as arrogant, but he's just shy.
  • Be careful how you word it — you don't want to come across as demanding.
  • In interviews, candidates who ask questions come across as more engaged.

CA: donar la impressió de / fer l'efecte de

ES: dar la impresión de / parecer

About the impression given, not the reality. Followed by an adjective or 'as a…'.

blocks.title: tailor something to
blocks.html:
verb + preposition

  • Tailor your CV to each job — the generic version gets ignored.
  • The course is tailored to the needs of adult learners.
  • Advice has to be tailored to the individual; blanket rules rarely help.

CA: adaptar (a mida) a

ES: adaptar a la medida de

From tailoring clothes. Very often passive: 'be tailored to'.

blocks.title: a steep learning curve
blocks.html:
adjective + noun

  • The first month was a steep learning curve — I'd never used that software.
  • New doctors face a steep learning curve in their first year on the wards.
  • Any career change involves a steep learning curve, but the pay-off can be considerable.

CA: una corba d'aprenentatge molt pronunciada

ES: una curva de aprendizaje muy pronunciada

'Steep' means hard and fast, not slow. Common error: *a high learning curve.
